content.text:
## Summary of Investigation

I reviewed the fix commit (`983a95f4e4`) in detail. Structurally, it does one thing almost 25 times over: it takes an existing `IS_DISTINCT_FROM` scalar operator implementation that only supported the `NULL_FLAG` calling convention (value + `boolean isNull` pairs), and refactors it into a static nested class with two methods — the original `NULL_FLAG` method, plus a new sibling method using the `BLOCK_POSITION` convention (`Block`, `int position` pairs) that operates directly on blocks without boxing through `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue`.

Critically, the container-type operators (`ArrayDistinctFromOperator`, `MapDistinctFromOperator`, `RowDistinctFromOperator`, used for comparing arrays/maps/rows of arbitrary element types, including nested arrays and `DECIMAL`) are switched from invoking their element-type dependency via `NULL_FLAG` + `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue(type.getJavaType())` boxing, to invoking it via `BLOCK_POSITION` (`invokeExact(block, position, block, position)`), and the new tests added in this commit specifically exercise exactly these paths (`ARRAY[DECIMAL...]`, nested `ARRAY[ARRAY[...]]`).

I traced the history of `ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java`, `MapDistinctFromOperator.java`, and `RowDistinctFromOperator.java` with `git log --follow`. All three files were created together in a single commit, `2fc72b7ce4051c30313bcc865eb74824f751670b` (Igor Demura, "replace bytecode-generated `IsDistinctFromCodeGenerator` with annotation-based scalar operators"). That commit:
- Deleted `IsDistinctFromCodeGenerator.java` (the old bytecode-gen approach for `IS_DISTINCT_FROM`).
- Introduced the annotation/`OperatorDependency`-based `IS_DISTINCT_FROM` operators for every primitive type plus `ArrayDistinctFromOperator`, `MapDistinctFromOperator`, and `RowDistinctFromOperator`, all built exclusively around the `NULL_FLAG` convention and `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue(type.getJavaType())` boxing for recursing into element types.

This is the architectural origin of the pattern that `983a95f4e4` later replaces/extends with `BLOCK_POSITION` support for complex/nested/parametric types (arrays-of-arrays, arrays/maps of `DECIMAL`, etc.) — i.e., it's the commit that put the codebase into the state the fix commit had to correct/extend.

I want to be upfront about the limits of this conclusion: most of the logic in the fix commit is additive (new overloaded methods with the same boolean logic as the existing `NULL_FLAG` methods), not a correction of clearly wrong arithmetic/comparisons. I could not, through static reading alone (no network/build available to actually run the old tests against the pre-fix code), prove a concrete wrong-result or crash scenario that the old `2fc72b7ce4`-era code produced for the new test cases — the `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue` + `MethodHandle.invoke` (auto-boxing) path appears logically capable of producing correct results for the scenarios in the added tests, just less efficiently (there's an explicit TODO comment in `JoinCompiler.java` referencing exactly this "block+position calling convention" gap as a known performance hack, not a correctness bug). So this could also be read as primarily a performance/feature enablement commit rather than a fix for a specific regression — I flag this as a meaningful source of uncertainty.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 2fc72b7ce4051c30313bcc865eb74824f751670b

## Reasoning
(1) I examined the fix commit's diff and found it uniformly restructures ~20 `IS_DISTINCT_FROM` operator implementations (one per type) from a single `NULL_FLAG`-only method into a nested class exposing both the original `NULL_FLAG` method and a new `BLOCK_POSITION` method. The new regression tests added (`TestArrayOperators`, `TestDecimalOperators`) specifically target nested arrays and decimal arrays going through `ArrayDistinctFromOperator`/`MapDistinctFromOperator`, which recurse into element-type `IS_DISTINCT_FROM` implementations via an `OperatorDependency`. I used `git log --follow` on `ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java`, `MapDistinctFromOperator.java`, and `RowDistinctFromOperator.java` to find their origin, which converged on a single commit.

(2) Commit `2fc72b7ce4` introduced these three container-type operators (replacing the older bytecode-generated `IsDistinctFromCodeGenerator`) using a design that recurses into element comparisons only via the `NULL_FLAG` convention, unboxing values with `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue(type.getJavaType())`. This design never provided a `BLOCK_POSITION`-based path, which is exactly the capability `983a95f4e4` retrofits across the entire type system (confirmed by the explicit TODO/hack comment already present in `JoinCompiler.java`: "The plan is to allow scalar function to optionally provide an additional implementation using Block+position calling convention... At that point, we'll be able to fully deprecate Type.equalTo").

(3) Evidence: (a) all three container-operator files trace back to the same single commit `2fc72b7ce4`; (b) that commit's diff shows it replacing the previous bytecode-gen `IS_DISTINCT_FROM` mechanism with exactly the `NULL_FLAG`/`readNativeValue` pattern that `983a95f4e4` dismantles; (c) the new tests in the fix commit are explicitly commented as "exercises block-position convention implementation" for array/decimal types handled by the operators created in `2fc72b7ce4`.

**Uncertainty:** I was not able to execute the pre-fix test suite (no network/build available in this sandboxed, read-only investigation) to directly confirm a wrong-result or crash in the `2fc72b7ce4`-era code for the newly added test cases. The bulk of the fix commit's logic is additive/parallel rather than a correction of an arithmetic/boolean mistake, so this could alternatively be characterized as a performance/feature-completion commit rather than a fix for a discrete correctness bug with a single clear origin. If a narrower, more conclusively "wrong logic" root cause exists, I was unable to isolate it from static analysis alone, and `2fc72b7ce4` should be treated as my best-supported but not fully certain candidate.
